acceptance_criteria: The CIET v3 loop runs entirely on OPCPFluidArray with no TUAS fluid arrays in its path; the known TUAS defects above are either avoided or explicitly inherited-and-documented, not silently carried.
description:
The core migration of this epic.

OPCPFluidArray lives in crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop/src/openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/ and is already consumed by tampines-steam-tables, so there is a working precedent to copy rather than a new integration to invent. Read that consumer first.

Scope: the CIET three-branch-plus-DRACS loop's fluid arrays move from TUAS's one_d_fluid_array_with_lateral_coupling to OPCPFluidArray, keeping the lateral-coupling behaviour the CIET components depend on.

DO NOT silently drop TUAS from tampines' dependencies as part of this - other tampines code and examples still use it, and the CIET regression tests being ported ARE TUAS tests. Whether tampines eventually sheds the TUAS dependency is a separate decision.

Watch for the known TUAS defects already tracked, so they are not faithfully reproduced into v3: op-4542 (Wakao correlation has swapped exponents, 5.84x divergence at Re=1000), op-lmye (CIET heater v2 feeds hydraulic-diameter Reynolds into a particle-diameter Wakao correlation), op-j7d0 (SolidColumn cylindrical-shell end control volumes built from a solid rod).
title: CIET v3: replace the TUAS array backend with OPCPFluidArray

description:
Maintainer direction while dogfooding (2026-09-02), explicitly scoped to 'the next version', not now.

'If multiple people use kovan, I want them to be able to collaborate.' Today kovan is single-user: one clone, one operator, Git as the only sync (Save Repository = commit; push/pull is manual under Advanced). For a shared research group:

- concurrent editing of the same paper's Markdown / artifacts without stomping (builds on op-hodx's merge-conflict handling),
- awareness of who wrote / reviewed which artifact (the `author`/`reviewed` fields exist; surface them),
- a workflow for proposing vs. accepting changes (review before merge),
- possibly a lightweight sync server option beyond raw Git, but Git-native stays the floor (issue #35 north star: 'rm -rf .kovan must always be safe').

Non-goal for the first cut: real-time CRDT co-editing. Start with async, Git-branch-based collaboration done well. Relates to op-9vo6, op-hodx, op-gw9r (literature submodule split).
title: kovan: multi-user collaboration (next version)
